title: Binary Search
statement: Find target in sorted array using binary search.
inputOutputContract: Input n target, followed by sorted n integers with unique values. Output 0-based index or -1.

mistakes.hint1: Inspect the excludes last candidate behavior in binarySearch; the current algorithm is close, but one operation changes its result.
mistakes.hint2: Start by tracing T3 manually. Watch array indices / comparisons / loop boundaries / return values at each iteration or recursive return.
mistakes.hint3: Check the invariant of binarySearch: Maintain inclusive left/right boundaries, update past mid, and return the actual 0-based index.
mistakes.hint4: Concentrate on the expression or branch that controls this mistake: `while (left < right)`. What does it do on the failing input?
mistakes.hint5: Compare the intermediate state with the expected output of T3. The mistake is in excludes last candidate, not merely formatting.
mistakes.hint6: Adjust the faulty operation so that it follows this rule: Maintain inclusive left/right boundaries, update past mid, and return the actual 0-based index.
mistakes.hint7: A targeted correction is to replace `while (left < right)` with `while (left <= right)` in binarySearch, then retest T1–T6.
